author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons’ request to deregister as a non-bank lender, according to two people familiar with the decision. The outcome leaves the closely held parent of several major Indian companies nearer to a possible stock-market listing.

Tata Sons had asked to give up its classification as a core investment company. RBI rules can require non-bank lenders with assets above 1 trillion rupees, or access to public funds, to list. Tata Sons reported standalone assets of 1.75 trillion rupees as of March 2025. The central bank communicated its decision in a letter Saturday, the sources said.

The holding company controls businesses including Tata Consultancy Services, Tata Motors, Tata Steel and Air India, and has sought to remain private. Listing pressure has also come from Shapoorji Pallonji Group, its second-largest shareholder. Tata Trusts owns 66% of Tata Sons. The RBI, Tata Sons and Tata Trusts did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and no listing timetable has been announced.
dek: India’s central bank rejected the holding company’s bid to shed its non-bank lender registration, according to two sources.
headline: RBI rejection moves Tata Sons closer to potential public listing
